headline: Image-derived metrics tied to explicit physical models of tissue and vascular mechanics
label: Quantitative Cell Mechanobiology Modelling
summary: Explicit mechanistic models are now being fed by quantitative image and micro-CT readouts across vascular, corneal, and tissue systems.
synthesis: The common thread is the explicit coupling of quantitative, physically defined variables to biological structure. Cornealia derives collective-order and intercellular-force metrics from donor corneal endothelial images and reports density-dependent reorganization. The vertex-flow model shows that hyaluronic acid osmotic pressure in intercellular space can drive lumen formation, budding, and branching, placing a mechanical driver directly in the morphogenesis model. The pulmonary arterial pipeline extracts geometric, persistent-homology, and shape features from micro-CT to classify hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension, while Multiscale MIGHT extends an inverse-Gaussian mixture model to closed-loop branched vessel networks with organ clearance and molecule degradation. What is new is the pairing of measured structure with transport and mechanical mechanism. The items are preprints and do not report experimental validation of model predictions.
